articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Croacia y España en el Stadion Poljud correspondiente a la jornada 4 del Grupo 3 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: Croacia afronta esta cuarta jornada de la Nations League después de sufrir la mayor goleada de su historia frente a Inglaterra. El conjunto balcánico llega, por tanto, obligado a reaccionar después de un resultado especialmente doloroso y con la necesidad de recuperar sensaciones. Enfrente tendrá a una España que continúa liderando el grupo y con una racha de invencibilidad que no parece tener fin. Favorito para el partido entre Croacia y España La selección española viene de lograr una victoria sufrida frente a la República Checa. Un resultado que le permite mantenerse asentada en lo más alto de la clasificación. Además, el combinado de Luis de la Fuente cuenta con el precedente del partido de ida, en el que goleó a Croacia. Las casas de apuestas conceden un claro favoritismo a España: Codere ofrece una cuota de 9.00 por la victoria croata, 5.50 por el empate y 1.28 por el triunfo español. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción interesante en las apuestas deportivas. Especialmente, teniendo en cuenta la dinámica de ambas selecciones. Croacia ha cumplido este pronóstico en dos de sus tres partidos de esta Nations League, mientras que España lo ha hecho en todos sus encuentros. Además, ambos equipos consiguieron ver portería en el enfrentamiento de ida, lo que refuerza la posibilidad de volver a encontrar goles en las dos áreas. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.80 por el 'sí' y de 1.90 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles presenta una tendencia todavía más clara. En todos los partidos disputados por Croacia en esta Nations League se han superado los 2.5 goles totales. Exactamente, el mismo registro que presenta España. Esta circunstancia también se produjo en el encuentro de ida, en el que el conjunto español se impuso con un marcador amplio. Todo ello apunta hacia un nuevo duelo con posibilidades de superar la línea de goles. Codere paga a 1.45 que se marquen más de 2.5 goles y a 2.60 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners ofrece, en cambio, una tendencia bastante más contenida. En ninguno de los partidos disputados por Croacia en esta Nations League se han superado los 9.5 lanzamientos de esquina, un registro que también se repite en todos los encuentros de España. Además, el partido de ida entre ambos combinados terminó con un total de ocho córners, por debajo de la línea planteada para este encuentro. Codere ofrece una cuota de 1.88 por que se superen los 9.5 córners y de 1.75 por que haya menos.

articles.title: ¿Qué pasa con Sinner?
articles.standfirst: El italiano se perderá lo que queda de temporada y reaparecerá en el Open de Australia si su lesión en la rodilla desaparece
articles.summary: El italiano se perderá lo que queda de temporada y reaparecerá en el Open de Australia si su lesión en la rodilla desaparece
articles.body: El tenis masculino va a cerrar 2026 con un giro inesperado. Jannik Sinner ha anunciado hoy que su temporada ha terminado y que se someterá a un tratamiento en la rodilla derecha. Se perderá el Six Kings Slam, Viena, París, las ATP Finals de Turín y la Copa Davis en Bolonia, y verá cómo Alexander Zverev le arrebata el número uno antes de fin de año. A la vez, Carlos Alcaraz, tras su travesía con la lesión de muñeca, ha vuelto a ganar un torneo hoy 227 días después, por lo que el mercado en las casas de apuestas del primer Grand Slam de 2027 ha quedado más abierto que nunca. El último partido de Sinner fue la final de Wimbledon, que ganó precisamente a Zverev. Desde entonces, las molestias en la rodilla le han hecho renunciar a Toronto, Cincinnati, el US Open y Pekín. Su decisión de parar, tomada junto a los médicos, tiene sentido a largo plazo, pero deja un interrogante enorme: cuando llegue enero, habrá pasado medio año sin competir. Zverev, entretanto, llega lanzado. El alemán ganó Roland Garros por primera vez y después el US Open ante Ben Shelton, además de perder la final de Wimbledon. Con dos Grand Slams en el año, 53 victorias y un ranking que le colocará en lo más alto, es una amenaza real. La otra gran noticia es la de Alcaraz. El murciano ha superado a Jiri Lehecka por 7-6(4) y 6-4 en la final del ATP 500 de Tokio, su primer título en 227 días, desde Doha, en febrero. Había ganado el Open de Australia ese mismo año, pero una lesión de muñeca le apartó cuatro meses y medio de las pistas tras la final de Montecarlo ante Sinner. Tokio es su tercer título de 2026, y confirma que su regreso es sólido. El mercado de las apuestas deportivas ha digerido las noticias con una mezcla de respeto y prudencia. En la mayoría de casas, Sinner sigue siendo el favorito a cuota 2.00, mientras que Alcaraz se mueve entre 2.20 y 2.50 (esta última en Tonybet y Betfair). La excepción es Bwin, que invierte el orden: 2.30 para Sinner y 2.20 para Alcaraz. Zverev es el siguiente, a 7.00 en Bwin y 8.00 en el resto, y Djokovic cierra el grupo a 17.00, salvo en Bwin, donde baja hasta 10.00. A favor del italiano juega su historial en Australia, donde llegará como ganador en dos ocasiones, y su capacidad para rendir al máximo tras largas pausas. En contra, las incógnitas físicas. Una rodilla que ha obligado a cancelar cuatro torneos y a pasar por un tratamiento no suele resolverse de forma lineal, y el italiano llegará a Melbourne sin ritmo de competición. El caso de Alcaraz demuestra que un parón largo no condena, pero también que el regreso lleva tiempo, ya que tardó cinco semanas en volver a ganar.

articles.title: Why Pittsburgh Penguins star Evgeni Malkin broke tradition following Alex Ovechkin’s Washington Capitals NHL retirement announcement
articles.summary: Evgeni Malkin speaks out following Alex Ovechkin's retirement announcement, marking a significant moment in their rivalry and the NHL's history. Discover the implications for both players and the Pittsburgh Penguins as the Capitals star sets to end his legendary career.
articles.body: The announcement immediately became one of the biggest NHL updates of the week. Alex Ovechkin confirmed that the 2026-27 season will be his final campaign with the Washington Capitals, bringing his 22-year NHL career toward its conclusion. The news also carried significance for the Pittsburgh Penguins, who have shared one of the league’s most recognizable rivalries with Washington throughout the careers of Ovechkin and Evgeni Malkin.For Evgeni Malkin, the announcement prompted an unusual decision. The Pittsburgh Penguins star broke his established routine of not speaking with reporters after morning skates, choosing instead to discuss Ovechkin and what his retirement means for their generation of NHL players.Evgeni Malkin spoke about Alex Ovechkin’s retirementEvgeni Malkin said Alex Ovechkin’s retirement will be difficult to see because of what the Washington Capitals captain has accomplished for his team and the NHL. Malkin also wished his longtime rival and friend good health during his final season.Malkin’s decision reflected the significance of Ovechkin’s announcement. For roughly two decades, the Pittsburgh Penguins center has generally avoided speaking to reporters following morning skates. Monday’s retirement news was important enough for him to change that routine.The two players have been connected since the 2004 NHL Draft. Ovechkin was selected No. 1 overall by the Washington Capitals, while Malkin went second to the Pittsburgh Penguins. Their careers subsequently developed alongside one another, creating years of memorable regular-season and playoff matchups.Malkin acknowledged that the relationship between the two Russian stars was not always perfect. However, he said past disagreements are behind them and emphasized that they have become good friends who support each other and their families.That evolution adds another dimension to the Penguins-Capitals rivalry. What began with two highly touted Russian prospects being selected first and second in the same draft eventually became a relationship marked by competition, mutual respect and friendship.What does Ovechkin’s final season mean for Pittsburgh?The Washington Capitals and Pittsburgh Penguins are scheduled to meet four times during the 2026-27 regular season. Their first meeting comes Wednesday in Washington, making the matchup particularly significant given Ovechkin’s retirement announcement.Malkin said games against Ovechkin have always felt special and acknowledged that the eventual retirement will be a sad moment. The remaining matchups now carry added importance because they represent some of the final opportunities for two players who entered the NHL in the same era to face one another.Malkin also offered an intriguing reflection about his own future. At 40, he acknowledged that this could potentially be his final NHL season as well, although he emphasized that he still loves playing hockey. That uncertainty gives the Penguins-Capitals meetings another storyline to follow throughout the season.The immediate focus, however, remains on Ovechkin. articles.title: Victor Wembanyama: NBA star trains with rugby club
articles.summary: NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama says he was inspired by the unity and camaraderie of rugby after spending time with French second tier side Provence.
articles.body:
NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama says he was inspired by the unity and camaraderie of rugby after spending part of his summer off-season training with French second tier side Provence.

The 22-year-old Frenchman, who is 7ft 4in and 16st 11lbs, is known for his off-beat search for ways to improve his game. He spent a fortnight focusing on physical and mental strength with Shaolin monks in China in 2025. , external

Footage shows Wembanyama , external hitting tackle pads, going through passing drills, taking part in a line-out and looming over the rest of the Provence team in a huddle before a pre-season friendly in August.

He was also filmed sharing a dressing-room embrace with former England international Teimana Harrison, who won five England caps in 2016 and now plays for Provence.

"It was a great experience, seeing the team spirit they have over there," said Wembanyama, , external who was joined on the trip by San Antonio Spurs' team-mate Harrison Barnes.

"It was very inspiring to see the relationship between team-mates, coaches and fans. The training was really hard, really good for stability, movement patterns and developing strength, but I am more grateful for the experience of how I was welcomed there.

"I have never been welcomed anywhere like this. I wasn't part of the team but they treated me like I was. I want to do it again."

Wembanyama combined his work with Provence with hosting his Hoop Gambit event, in which participants play games of chess and basketball, in his hometown of Le Chesnay.

Wembanyama's Spurs fell just short of the NBA Championship earlier this year, going down 4-1 to the New York Knicks in June.

Provence, who previously have been represented by Wales internationals George North and Tomas Francis, have begun their season and search for promotion to the Top 14 well, winning their first five league games.

articles.title: Así quedó la grama de El Campín tras los conciertos de BTS en Bogotá: la decisión que afecta a Santa Fe
articles.standfirst: Preocupación en Bogotá: filtran imágenes de cómo quedó el césped de El Campín tras el paso de BTS
articles.summary: Preocupación en Bogotá: filtran imágenes de cómo quedó el césped de El Campín tras el paso de BTS
articles.body: Los cuatro conciertos consecutivos de la agrupación surcoreana BTS en Bogotá marcaron un hito sin precedentes para la industria del entretenimiento en Colombia, reuniendo a más de 160.000 espectadores en el estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín. Sin embargo, tras el retiro de las estructuras del escenario y de la teleras de protección, la imagen de la gramilla ha generado inquietud entre los aficionados al fútbol capitalino. El uso intensivo durante cuatro jornadas consecutivas, sumado a las pesadas infraestructuras de montaje y al constante tráfico de personas en el área de cancha, dejó evidentes secuelas en el césped: Ante el deterioro visual del terreno de juego, Sencia —la APP encargada de la administración y renovación del escenario deportivo— activó de inmediato un plan de contingencia agrónomico para recuperar la gramilla en un plazo máximo de 10 días. El plan de restauración comprende las siguientes fases: La principal urgencia recae en la reprogramación de los compromisos de Independiente Santa Fe y Millonarios. Aunque las directivas de Sencia aseguran que la cancha estará apta para el desarrollo del FPC dentro del lapso fijado, la evolución climática de Bogotá durante los próximos días será crucial para determinar si los equipos capitalinos podrán disputar sus compromisos en las fechas programadas o si se requerirán ajustes de última hora en el calendario. Por lo pronto se estima que mientras dure la recuperación de la grama de el Campín, Santa Fe traslade su compromiso contra Fortaleza, que tendrá lugar el próximo 11 de octubre, al estadio Municipal de Techo.

articles.title: Saints vs. Falcons Game MVP
articles.summary: The fans showed up for the Saints, unfortunately the game didn't go as expected.
articles.body:
In all honesty, after getting your teeth kicked in the way the Saints just did in primetime, there really isn't a player of the game. It is worth noting that Chris Olave played great again, but that's not worth much when the team gets embarrassed the way it just did.

The true MVPs of this game, however, were the fans.

Shoutout to the entire city of New Orleans, which was on 10 from the moment the sun came up. New Orleans was ready and excited for what this game represented: the 20-year celebration of the reopening of the Superdome after Hurricane Katrina.

The atmosphere inside the Dome at kickoff was electric. I spoke with former Saints wide receiver Lance Moore after the game, and he said the Dome felt like the Dome again. And that is exactly what it should be.

The fans were ready to roll. The excitement was there, and every single one of you, whether you were at home, at work, or at the stadium, just wanted that moment to shout, "Who Dat!"

The Saints did a great job of having Steve Gleason lead the Who Dat chant at the start of the game, with his son by his side raising his hand. The emotions were nearly overwhelming as a fan, seeing all of the pageantry that went into this game. The former players from 20 years ago were present on the sideline for kickoff. It was beautiful to see.

All of that went away because, for the next three hours, the play on the field did not match the expectations and hope that Saints fans had going into the night.

Who Dat Nation, you all are this week's Canal Street Chronicles MVP.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton can overtake George Russell for second in F1 title race as Mercedes penalty opens the door in Singapore
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton has a real chance to take second place in the Formula 1 drivers' championship from George Russell this weekend. Mercedes has confirmed that Ru...
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton has a real chance to take second place in the Formula 1 drivers' championship from George Russell this weekend. Mercedes has confirmed that Russell will start Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix from the back of the grid, and the Ferrari driver trails him by just 22 points.

Mercedes confirmed that Russell needs a new power unit after his retirement in Malaysia, as GPBlog reported in Russell hit hard by PU change: heavy grid penalty confirmed for Singapore . The team has confirmed that Russell will take the new unit in Singapore and start from the back.

After Sepang, Kimi Antonelli leads on 320 points. Russell has 236 and Hamilton 214. Russell scored nothing after his late engine failure, while Hamilton finished third after battling back from the pack, with GPblog's analysis showing how Hamilton overruled Ferrari's pit wall at Sepang and how that recovery played out to give him some momentum heading to Singapore.

Singapore is the last Sprint weekend of 2026, so there are more points on offer than usual. The Sprint pays eight points to the winner down to one for eighth place, and a Grand Prix win is worth 25. That means one driver can score at most 33 points across the weekend. GPblog used the same figure to show how Antonelli can't be crowned in Singapore but also explained how it keeps Hamilton in the hunt for second place.

To move up to second outright, Hamilton has to score 23 points more than Russell. Beating him by 22 would only put them level. Even a perfect double would take Hamilton to 247 points, so if Russell scores 11 points or more, the Mercedes driver keeps second place for at least another round.

Here's how the points would shake out in the drivers' championship in Singapore

Hamilton wins both the Sprint and the Grand Prix (33 points): Russell must score 10 points or fewer.

Hamilton wins the Grand Prix and finishes third in the Sprint (31 points): Russell must score 8 points or fewer.

Hamilton finishes second in both races (25 points): Russell must score 2 points or fewer.

Hamilton finishes third in both races (21 points): not enough, because a pointless Russell would still lead him by one point.

Lewis Hamilton givin his team the okay in Singapore. Photo: RacePictures.

The Sprint is Russell's best chance to hold on

Russell gets one opportunity to protect his position before the penalty applies as the penalty will be served in Sunday's Grand Prix, not the Sprint, so on Saturday he will start from wherever he qualifies.

That could be key because Russell has been the strongest Sprint driver this season. He has won three of the five Sprints so far, in China, Canada and the Netherlands. If he wins on Saturday, Hamilton would need second place in the Sprint and victory on Sunday, and Russell would have to finish outside the points in the Grand Prix.

Sunday is a different story as overtaking at Marina Bay is notoriously difficult, which makes starting from the back a big handicap. Russell knows the circuit well, though: he won the 2025 Singapore Grand Prix from pole position, but this season it could be too great a task.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 5 Tight End Waiver Wire Targets: Prioritize T.J. Hockenson
articles.summary: T.J. Hockenson and these other two tight ends are worth targeting on the fantasy football waiver wire entering Week 5.
articles.body:
Some fantasy football managers are lucky enough to have Brock Bowers locked into their tight end spot, essentially giving them another wide receiver in the lineup. Aside from Bowers, Trey McBride remains a consistent source of fantasy production, and George Kittle is excelling in an efficient offense.

If you don't roster any of the premier TEs in fantasy football, which TEs should you target on the waiver wire in Week 5?

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros .

T.J. Hockenson turned back the clock a bit in Week 4, producing a TE1 finish with 24.9 fantasy points on 13 receptions and 119 receiving yards. The Kyler Murray-led aerial attack for the Minnesota Vikings is still in the adjustment phase, and Murray is building a decent rapport with Hockenson.

While Justin Jefferson will undoubtedly be the No. 1 target for Murray when he returns from injury, Hockenson can emerge as the No. 2 option ahead of Jordan Addison. Next up for Hockenson and the Vikings are the New Orleans Saints, who are 28th in dropback EPA (0.22) and 30th in dropback success rate (52.4%) allowed this season.

Brenton Strange logged a season-best 16.5 fantasy points in Week 4, tying Tucker Kraft as the TE5. While Strange is still just the TE21 in fantasy points per game (9.2) entering Week 5, he's part of an ultra-efficient passing attack with Trevor Lawrence dealing for the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Of the 25 TEs with 15-plus targets this season, Strange has the sixth-most yards per reception (11.9) and seventh-most yards per route run (1.86).

Both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins picked up injuries in Week 4 for the Cincinnati Bengals, and it remains to be seen what their statuses will be in Week 5 against the Miami Dolphins. If Chase and/or Higgins are sidelined on Sunday, Mike Gesicki stands out as a solid waiver-wire option.

Aside from this week's matchup being a revenge game for Gesicki, he's the TE13 in fantasy points per game (11.1) with 12-plus fantasy points in three of his first four starts in 2026.

articles.title: The 49ers will be without Kyle Juszczyk vs. Seahawks in Week 5
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers will be without FB Kyle Juszczyk versus the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks play a critical divisional game in Week 5 . They'll host their NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers at Lumen Field. The 3-1 Seahawks currently trail the perfect 4-0 49ers in the division.

Fortunately for the Seahawks, Kyle Shanahan's offense will be without a critical playmaker. Fullback Kyle Juszczyk will miss the Week 5 game versus Seattle. An MRI recently revealed that Juszczyk has a knee sprain and bone bruise that will sideline him for multiple weeks, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The 49ers offense is currently averaging 137.3 rushing yards per game. That ranks sixth-best in the entire NFL. Juszczyk is often a big reason why Coach Shanahan fields such an effective ground attack. Juszczyk consistently generates rushing lanes for Christian McCaffrey.

The Seahawks are dealing with injuries of their own. Head coach Mike Macdonald recently provided health updates on Leonard Williams and Zach Charbonnet. Getting Williams back for the 49ers game is critical to slowing down McCaffrey and the 49ers' rushing offense.

The NFC West is so competitive. The division title may be decided by the games between the Seahawks, 49ers, and Los Angeles Rams. The Seahawks won't exactly be sad to hear the 49ers won't have Juszczyk on Sunday.

articles.title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Won vs. the New York Jets
articles.summary: Chicago grinded out another home win this week without their start QB. @BryanOrenchuk shares his 3 reasons the Bears earned the W.
articles.body:
Welcome back to the fourth installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game.

In week 4, the Bears hosted the feisty New York Jets and controlled the game from start to finish, dominating the time of possession and coming away with a gritty win once again without Caleb Williams as he recovers from his hamstring injury. Here are my three reasons why they won.

Though the 2nd year player out of Rutgers has had one game where he had more rushing yards than the 149 he racked up on the ground against the Jets, and five games where he did so with more yards per carry than the 4.9 he had, he has never scored more than once like he did and never had 30 carries before either. Considering he was clearly the best player on the field for both teams, I will henceforth be referring to this performance as the "Monangai Game" until further notice.

What impressed me most about the New Jersey native was the nature by which his success came. He was getting met at or behind the line of scrimmage early in this one and ended the first half with only 49 yards rushing. But he seemed to get stronger as the game wore on, consistently bouncing off would-be tacklers or peeling away from them for extra yardage before sporadic bursts through the line for chunk gains. You could tell he was wearing on the defense and clearly Ben Johnson could tell as well considering he saw 30 carries to D'Andre Swift's 15. On a day where the Bears struggled to put the ball in the endzone and score TDs, Monangai seemed like the difference in this one and the main reason Chicago came away with a W. Shout out to the offensive line for continuing to pound away at the formidable Jets defensive line and the wide receivers and tight ends for committing to the gameplan as well. When you have a back like Monangai, you never know when he will break away and use your block for more yardage.

Speaking of best games, this was easily Rome's best game of the season as well. What stood out to me regarding Odunze's performance, aside from marveling at how a WR his size (6'3", 215lb) moves in and out of his breaks, was how seamlessly he caught the ball this week and the clutch nature of his catches. All game, it seemed like Rome was coming up big on 3rd down and was a large reason why we were able to move the ball down the field, especially in the first half before Monangai took over. Rome's 94 receiving yards paced both teams in this one, and he did so on just 7 targets with 6 catches for 15.7 yards per catch and a season-best 85.7 catch percentage. Rome played with confidence and power as both a pass-catcher and run-blocker, and his presence was felt throughout this win.

On a day when the offense struggled to find the endzone, especially in the red zone, it sure was nice to have such an automatic kicker on your side. Especially in the Windy City, with gusts coming off the lake as they do. Though none of his kicks were longer than 30 yards, Santos helped keep this game out of reach for a Jets comeback. Without Santos, I am not sure Ben elects to kick the FG which made it a three score game in the 4th quarter, which could have changed the entire outcome in this one. Ben trusts him, and his teammates do too, and it showed up this week.

What about you? Who or what caught your attention against the Jets?

articles.title: Fred Claire, Dodgers GM whose Kirk Gibson signing created iconic moment, dies
articles.summary: Fred Claire, who guided the Dodgers through a pivotal era and helped assemble the 1988 World Series winners, dies at the age of 91.
articles.body:
Fred Claire, the former Los Angeles Dodgers general manager whose signing of Kirk Gibson led to one of the most iconic moments in baseball history, died Monday, Oct. 5, the Dodgers announced. He was 91.

Claire took over the Dodgers franchise at a most tumultuous time - after longtime general manager and vice president Al Campanis was fired for racist remarks made on ABC's Nightline. His April 9, 1987 dismissal ended an era of front office stability while the Dodgers embarked on a fourth consecutive year missing the playoffs.

Claire, a former sportswriter and Dodgers PR man, was tabbed to run the front office. A pair of transactions in the year that followed shaped the Dodgers' eventual 1988 championship core: A three-way winter meetings trade with the Oakland Athletics and New York Mets that netted the Dodgers relievers Jesse Orosco and Jay Howell and shortstop Alfredo Griffin.

Those Dodgers won 94 games, stunned the Mets in the National League Championship Series and pulled an even bigger shocker in the 1988 World Series, beating the A's in five games despite a battered club that came to rely on ace Orel Hershiser and an itinerant band of ballplayers known as the "Stuntmen."

And they only had Gibson for one at-bat - but he made the most of it. Gibson's two-out, two-run, ninth-inning homer off peerless closer Dennis Eckersley delivered the Dodgers a Game 1 win and the 104-win A's never recovered.

Claire held his position for a decade, ushered out unceremoniously after Fox bought the club and dickered over the re-signing of Mike Piazza. Piazza's trade to the Florida Marlins was brokered above Claire's head. He was fired weeks later.

Claire remained a well-regarded baseball mind, and later in life documented his journey through cancer treatments , eventually penning an autobiography, "Extra Innings," that detailed his life in baseball and his battle against the disease.

He is survived by his wife Cheryl and children Jeff, Jennifer and Kim.

"The Dodgers are grieving the passing of Fred Claire, a longtime key fixture of our organization," said Stan Kasten, President and CEO of the Dodgers, in a statement released by the club. "Fred brought many victories and Dodger legends to our franchise, as well as a 1988 World Series title, and we are forever grateful for his leadership during such a memorable era. Our hearts go out to his wife Sheryl and his family."

articles.title: Excl: Arsenal in talks with Nicolas Jover over new deal
articles.summary: Arsenal have been in negotiations with Nicolas Jover over a contract extension during the international break, following Mikel Arteta’s agreement on a new de...
articles.body:
Arsenal have been in negotiations with Nicolas Jover over a contract extension during the international break, following Mikel Arteta's agreement on a new deal.

Daily Cannon understands that Andrea Berta has been leading negotiations with Arsenal set-piece coach Nicolas Jover over a new contract during the international break, with the club keen to extend the deals of Mikel Arteta's assistants.

Arsenal's staff and players remain very much aligned on the value of set-pieces, and the club are willing to recognise that with a good contract.

Previous reports at the start of the break had suggested that Arteta's backroom staff would sign four-year deals, in line with the manager's own reported new contract to 2030. But Daily Cannon's understanding is that talks were still ongoing during the break.

Jover has developed a special methodology for Arsenal's set-piece training and implementation, and the club clearly want to keep him around.

It's possible that Arsenal's desire to extend the contracts of all of Arteta's backroom staff is behind the delay in the announcement for the manager's own new deal.

Sami Mokbel had broken the news for the BBC on September 22nd that Arteta had agreed a new contract, bringing to an end negotiations that had been ongoing for a number of months.

Fabrizio Romano reported on Monday that Arteta is ready to put pen to paper, but that still doesn't seem to have happened at the time of writing.

With no official announcement and nothing formally signed, the only thing currently tying Arteta to Arsenal beyond the summer of 2027 is his verbal agreement with the club.

But given how well things have been going for all parties in 2026 so far, and with a substantial pay increase on the table, the expectation is that the formalities will be concluded soon.

articles.title: Juventus & Napoli to Address Their Midfields in January
articles.summary: Juventus and Napoli are making preparations ahead of January, and both teams aim to shore up their midfields because of some injury blows. The Bianconeri won...
articles.body:
Juventus and Napoli are making preparations ahead of January, and both teams aim to shore up their midfields because of some injury blows. The Bianconeri won't have Khephren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli for months, while Frank Anguissa and Scott McTominay have had some problems for the Partenopei .

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Old Lady is particularly keen on Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg. Luciano Spalletti wants a veteran leader. Former free agents Leon Goretzka and Frank Kessié have latched onto other clubs.

Olympique Marseille are in a financial crunch, so the Dane isn't untouchable despite being the captain and a pillar. Their new CEO Giovanni Carnevali has done a lot of business with the French club, signing Ismael Koné, Ulisses Garcia, and Darryl Bakola during his time with Sassuolo.

Napoli are also in the hunt for a midfielder, but they plan to go younger than Juventus. They have shortlisted Monaco's Mamadou Coulibaly. His physicality would come in handy. He has registered 4 goals and 7 assists in 47 matches with his current team.

The possible fallback is Union Saint-Gilloise's Adem Zorgane, who will turn 27 in January. He's a staple with Algeria and can handle multiple roles. The Azzurri are also keeping tabs on Dodo, who might depart Fiorentina for cheap to avoid a Bosman exit.

They are both in trouble in the role, and the Azzurri appear headed for a significant overhaul at the end of the campaign. They'd better start bringing in quality reinforcements as soon as they can, and they are already one man short. Hojbjerg would be a fine addition, but the buzz linking him to Serie A has never amounted to much in the past.

articles.title: Lakers insider reveals real reason why Wizards' Anthony Davis gained weight after latest comment
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Lakers NBA champion Anthony Davis revealed that he was having to gain weight to play center during his time with the organization. A Laker...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers are now in the Luka Doncic era, and the process of it started in early 2025. Doncic was playing with the Dallas Mavericks when the most shocking trade in NBA history went down.

The Lakers made a trade for Doncic that shipped out Anthony Davis.

"The Dallas Mavericks are trading Luka Doncic, Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis, Max Christie and a 2029 first-round pick, sources tell ESPN. Three-team deal that includes Utah," ESPN's Shams Charania posted.

This ended Davis' long tenure in LA, one where he played center for most of his career. Davis revealed that he had to gain weight to play center, and it just didn't work out with his body.

"The strength training I was doing because I knew I was playing center, like I'm going against Joel Embiid and Jokic. And I never like I've always played like 250. And that year I had got to like 265 and it was like I didn't like it. It was actually probably like 268 and I didn't like it. I'm like, bro, I can't play like this. I feel heavy. So I tried to cut during the season but when when you trying to do that while you playing this it was tough. And then that's when I went and was like hey man I want another big and all this stuff and you know it just didn't happen whatever," Davis said.

However, Lakers insider Anthony F. Irwin reported that Davis gained weight because he stopped working hard.

"AD didn't gain weight because the Lakers asked him to play center. He gained the weight because he stopped working as hard on keeping the weight off. He then had to play center because he couldn't move his feet quite as well and forgot how to shoot," Irwin posted.

This situation now has another layer to it, as a Lakers insider has called Davis out for not taking care of himself when it matters the most. Davis' tenure with LA did come to a screaming halt.

It seems like behind the scenes, Davis was doing whatever it took to get the Lakers to stop playing him at center. The more this drags on, the messier the relationship between the two seems to get.

articles.title: College football prediction market picks, upset bets for Week 6
articles.summary: Two Saturday clashes between unbeaten teams headline this week's six prediction market selections, with three more games kicking off Friday night out West.
articles.body:
Week 6 college football prediction market picks back Alabama, FIU, Washington and Utah State as favorites, while Iowa State and Nebraska carry upset paths built on injuries, soft schedules and steady market support.

The biggest swing came in Tuscaloosa, where No. 2 Georgia opened as a 3-point favorite before No. 6 Alabama flipped the line after a 56-23 win at Mississippi State. Both teams enter Saturday night's matchup at 5-0.

FIU and Utah State have drawn the steadiest support among this week's favorites, as both spreads have climbed 2.5 points since opening. Meanwhile, Iowa State and Nebraska have each gained at least 2.5 points as underdogs.

Florida International Panthers wide receiver Maguire Anderson (84) runs against the Penn State Nittany Lions | Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images

FIU's defense has allowed 58 points through four games and held LIU to a lone field goal in a 20-3 win before the bye. "Another win, so I won't apologize for a win , but we once again did not play our best football, specifically on offense," FIU coach Willie Simmons said after the game. The Panthers still convert 47% of their third downs, while New Mexico State allows opponents to convert 42% of the time.

Quarterback JJ Kohl, a 6-foot-7 transfer from App State, suffered a grade-one MCL sprain against LIU but practiced during the off week. He also leads Conference USA with six interceptions, and FIU turned it over three times in each loss to USF and Florida Atlantic. New Mexico State (2-3, 1-0) enters off a 21-point home win over Western Kentucky, but the Aggies also committed three turnovers in losses to Hawaii and New Mexico.

Washington Huskies quarterback Demond Williams Jr. (1) passes the ball against the USC Trojans | Griffin Hooper-Imagn Images

Iowa ran for 39 yards on 21 carries in Saturday's 31-14 home loss to Ohio State, and quarterback Hank Brown completed 12 of 27 passes for 132 yards before leaving with a mild sprain. Brown remains atop the depth chart , but the No. 20 Hawkeyes now face a short-week trip roughly 2,000 miles from Iowa City.

Washington (3-2, 0-2) has lost two straight by a combined seven points, including a 25-21 loss at USC decided by a 48-yard fumble return touchdown. The Huskies' rushing attack ranks 124th nationally , so Demond Williams Jr. has to carry the offense against a defense that allowed 8 points per game through September. Still, Washington's defense gives up 16.8 points per game, and the spread has moved from Washington -1.5 to -3 since opening.

Utah State Aggies wide receiver Eli Wood (7) celebrates after catching a touchdown pass from quarterback Grady Brosterhous (9) during the fourth quarter at Husky Stadium. | Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images

Utah State and Washington State are both 1-4 and 0-1 in Pac-12 play, but their results against a common opponent favor the Aggies. Utah State lost 16-14 at Washington, while Washington State fell 24-10 to the Huskies in its opener. The Cougars also lost 26-6 at home to Fresno State last week, and quarterback Caden Pinnick has five interceptions against three touchdown passes.

Utah State coach Bronco Mendenhall's team has its own problems after an opening loss to FCS Idaho State and a 37-18 defeat at Boise State. "I haven't cracked that code," Mendenhall said of his team's mistakes in Boise. However, receiver Eli Wood has 388 yards and four touchdowns, and the Aggies host a Washington State offense that has scored 13 points across its last two games.

Iowa State Cyclones running back Aiden Flora (21) breaks through the West Virginia Mountaineers' defense for a touchdown during the second half at Jack Trice Stadium. | Reese Strickland-Imagn Images

No. 8 BYU is 4-0, but last week's 17-10 win at TCU was tied 7-7 at halftime, and running back LJ Martin left with an injury . Quarterback Bear Bachmeier has 704 passing yards and six touchdown passes, and he scored twice on the ground in Fort Worth.

First-year Iowa State coach Jimmy Rogers' Cyclones (3-2) lost 16-13 at Iowa and 31-17 to Utah, then rebounded with a home win over West Virginia. Iowa State also leads the all-time series 5-1 and is 3-0 in Provo, though BYU won 41-27 in Ames last season. The spread has dropped four points since opening and the total has fallen to 46.5, which points toward the low-scoring game Iowa State needs.

Nebraska Cornhuskers wide receiver Jacory Barney Jr. (2), quarterback Anthony Colandrea (10), wide receiver Kwazi Gilmer (3) and running back Mekhi Nelson (13) wait with teammates | Dylan Widger-Imagn Images

Nebraska (5-0, 2-0) is off to its best start since 2016 and has scored at least 30 points in every game. Quarterback Anthony Colandrea accounted for 346 yards and three touchdowns in a 48-23 win over Maryland, including a career-high 108 rushing yards. "We're going to make people defend our quarterback ," Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said Monday.

No. 7 Indiana carries the nation's longest active winning streak at 21 games, and quarterback Josh Hoover has 15 touchdown passes without an interception. However, Jeff Sagarin's ratings place the Hoosiers' schedule 103rd nationally and the Cornhuskers' 111th, so neither team has faced an opponent like this one. The spread has also dropped 2.5 points since opening, and Indiana's defense hasn't seen a quarterback run game like Colandrea's.

Alabama Crimson Tide wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams (1) celebrates with offensive lineman Jackson Lloyd (77) and quarterback Keelon Russell (12) after scoring a touchdown against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | Petre Thomas-Imagn Images

Alabama hasn't scored fewer than 45 points in a game this season, and Keelon Russell has thrown 10 touchdown passes in his last three starts. The sophomore quarterback is completing 71.2% of his passes for 1,414 yards, 11 touchdowns and two interceptions, which moved him into the top three of this SI Heisman Trophy tracker .

Georgia hasn't allowed more than 20 points in a game and has outscored opponents 70-7 in the first quarter. "This version has just jumped all over people ," Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said of the Bulldogs.

But Georgia hasn't won in Tuscaloosa since 2007, and Alabama's defense leads the SEC with 13 takeaways. DeBoer's teams have won two of three meetings with Georgia coach Kirby Smart, including a 24-21 win last season before Georgia took the SEC Championship Game 28-7.

Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER.

articles.title: F1 Driver Valtteri Bottas Posts Video, Photos Amid 217-Mile Bike Ride to Singapore Grand Prix
articles.summary: Formula 1 driver Valtteri Bottas is taking the scenic route while traveling to race for Cadillac in the Singapore Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Formula 1 driver Valtteri Bottas is taking the scenic route while traveling to race for Cadillac in the Singapore Grand Prix.

Bottas is biking 217 miles from Malaysia to Singapore ahead of Sunday's race, according to BBC Sport's Adam Millington .

The Finnish driver and gravel biker has shared photos and videos from throughout the journey since departing last Sunday.

Bottas announced in August he had qualified for the UCI Gravel World Championships, although the championship race overlaps with the Singapore Grand Prix.

He began biking on his own last Sunday just hours after the completion of the Bahrain Grand Prix in the Malaysian town of Sepang, per Millington.

The 37-year-old is set to arrive in Singapore in time to speak to reporters Thursday, according to Millington.

Bottas lost his seat with Sauber in 2025 and served in a reserve role for Mercedes before signing with Cadillac ahead of the 2026 season.

Still without a point and with eight DNFs so far this season, Bottas is looking to bounce back in Singapore after spinning into gravel and retiring on the ninth lap of the Bahrain Grand Prix.

articles.title: Arch Manning vs. John Mateer: Inside The Red River Rivalry QB Battle
articles.summary: Arch Manning vs. John Mateer sets up a fascinating Red River Rivalry QB matchup, with surprising similarities between the two quarterbacks. FOX Sports' Brady Quinn breaks down the matchup.
articles.body: There’s nothing like a college football rivalry game. Legacies are made, bragging rights are claimed and memories are created. The experience for all involved is unique, and it’s one of the reasons college football is the greatest sport on the planet. This week’s Red River Rivalry is no different. No. 1 Texas will take on an Oklahoma team still searching for answers on offense, setting the stage for a fascinating quarterback matchup. On one side is Texas QB Arch Manning, an early-season Heisman contender, carrying the weight of the Manning name and leading the No. 1-ranked team in the nation. On the other side is John Mateer, a signal-caller trying to find his footing and help get Oklahoma’s season back on track. But here’s the interesting part: Take a closer look at the numbers between Manning and Mateer, and maybe they aren’t so far apart? I'm going to dive into this matchup between quarterbacks and explain what Oklahoma can do to get Mateer back on track, as well as how Manning can better utilize a redone cheat code he has on his side. Red River Rivalry: Manning vs. Mateer Manning is the field general leading an undefeated Texas team, and whether you believe quarterback wins should count as a "stat" or not, an unbeaten record tends to give a QB the benefit of the doubt. But here’s where the comparison gets interesting: Mateer has statistically played better in Oklahoma’s biggest games at Michigan and Georgia than Manning has in Texas’ marquee matchups against Ohio State and Tennessee this season. That doesn’t tell the whole story, though. Manning’s numbers have been hurt by some costly drops from his receivers. Texas has had seven passes dropped this season, nearly twice as many as Oklahoma, and a couple of those misses have had a significant impact. Junior wide receiver Ryan Wingo leads Texas with three drops and should have had an easy touchdown against Ohio State after getting wide open down the field. In that same game, transfer wide receiver Cam Coleman also found himself wide open, only for what should have been a spectacular diving catch to somehow turn into a circus interception for the Buckeyes. When a quarterback puts the ball in the right spot and his guys make the play, it builds trust and rhythm. Those two plays alone could have dramatically changed not only the game itself, but perhaps the way we’re talking about Manning’s season through five weeks. While Manning has been impacted by costly drops from his pass-catchers, Mateer has struggled to anticipate throws and find a consistent rhythm with his wide receivers. In fact, on Mateer’s longest touchdown pass of the season — a 53-yard strike to senior wideout Isaiah Sategna III in Oklahoma’s 14-6 win over New Mexico — the quarterback admitted he didn’t even realize Sategna was wide open until he heard the crowd react to how wide open he was. Yes, statistically, Manning and Mateer appear to be relatively close. But how they’ve gotten there tells a much different story — and it’s a story Oklahoma will have to hope it has figured out over the course of the bye week if the Sooners want to take home the "Golden Hat." Mateer Needs More Answers What’s most concerning is that this is Year 4 for Mateer in Ben Arbuckle’s offense. At this point, Mateer should be able to run this offense blindfolded. The fact that he’s struggling to play from the pocket and anticipate throws is an issue, but it’s not all on Mateer. Bottom line: Arbuckle has to devise a better plan to help his wide receivers create separation. According to PFF, Oklahoma has the fewest targets with separation in the SEC, and that shows up on film. Incorporate more bunches, stacks and pre-snap shifts and motion to help create leverage for the intended targets. Give Mateer a pre-snap coverage indicator by displacing a running back or tight end outside the formation. That simple adjustment forces the defense to show its hand: Is it playing man or zone? Getting that answer in the passing game is half the battle. If it’s man, you typically have the matchup you’re looking for or a concept designed to create an opening for a receiver. If it’s zone, you know the progression you’re reading and which routes should be available based on the leverage of the defenders. Those coverage indicators can make a quarterback more confident and decisive after the snap. And for Mateer, that might be exactly what Oklahoma needs. Manning Can Lean on Coleman Manning’s biggest advantage in the red zone might be the size of Coleman on the outside. Coleman’s 6-foot-3 frame has made him a big-time red-zone target for Manning this season, with three of his four receiving touchdowns coming inside the 20-yard line. It’s easy to see why. Coleman has tremendous length and the ability to stop, adjust and high-point the football at a moment’s notice. For a quarterback, that’s a huge advantage because you don’t necessarily have to be perfect with your ball placement. You just have to give your guy a chance. I had the pleasure of playing with two big-bodied wide receivers at Notre Dame in Maurice Stovall and Jeff Samardzija. The goal was simple: Once you got into the red zone, find a way to isolate one of them and give him a catchable ball so he could use his size and adjust to it. It didn’t always have to be pretty, but it did have to be catchable. Their size advantage typically led to one of three outcomes: a touchdown, defensive pass interference or, at worst, an incompletion. That’s the predicament a player like Coleman creates for a defense. Do you bracket him and try to eliminate him? Or do you leave him one-on-one, knowing you also have to account for the run game and the possibility of Manning pulling the ball down and running? Pick your poison. One matchup I’ll be watching closely is Oklahoma cornerback Eli Bowen against Coleman. Bowen is listed at 5-foot-9, giving Coleman a significant size advantage on the perimeter. Don’t be surprised if Texas looks for that matchup when it gets into the red zone this weekend. One Name To Know … Kenny Minchey, Kentucky If you listen closely, you can hear the whispers about a QB playing down in the Bluegrass State. Kentucky is best known for its horse racing, bourbon and college basketball. But there’s a new signal-caller turning heads. Kenny Minchey began his collegiate career at Notre Dame, where patience became a prerequisite. He redshirted, then watched two transfer quarterbacks leapfrog him and become QB1. His chance to compete for the starting job finally came ahead of the 2025 season, when he battled CJ Carr for the position. Minchey ultimately lost that competition and settled into a backup role, finishing the season with 26 pass attempts, completing 20 of them, before deciding it was time to find his next opportunity. The transfer portal window opened Jan. 4, and Minchey immediately committed to Nebraska, only to flip his commitment 24 hours later following a phone call with new Kentucky head coach Will Stein. Former Kentucky starting quarterback Cutter Boley had entered the transfer portal, creating a clear path for Minchey to become QB1. Stein and Minchey haven’t looked back since. The Wildcats are 4-1, with big road wins over Texas A&M and South Carolina, including a dramatic overtime finish against the Gamecocks. Minchey has quickly established himself as one of the SEC’s top quarterbacks, throwing for 11 touchdowns with just one interception this season. Kentucky received the most AP votes of any team outside this week’s Top 25, but voters still appear hesitant to fully buy in. That hesitation is understandable after the Wildcats’ second-half collapse in a blowout loss to Alabama in Week 2. A win over LSU this weekend could change that narrative entirely and those whispers will turn to shouts if Minchey keeps playing well. What I'm Watching … Nebraska vs. Indiana A BIG ONE in the BIG TEN! And I'll be there as Big Noon Kickoff heads to Lincoln this weekend for the Big Ten showdown. Nebraska is searching for its first win over a ranked opponent in 30 games, while Indiana is defending its national title after beating six ranked opponents during its perfect 16-0 season last year. Neither team has faced a particularly challenging schedule, but both are 5-0 and led by transfer quarterbacks who have been perfect fits for their respective systems. Josh Hoover, the former TCU signal-caller, arrived in Bloomington with more experience and production than just about any quarterback in college football. That experience has shown up in his quick decision-making and timing. Hoover has erased concerns about turnovers, throwing 15 touchdowns with zero interceptions. I think Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and offensive coordinator Mike Shanahan have done it again. Meanwhile, Nebraska wanted an experienced quarterback with more dual-threat ability after parting ways with former five-star Dylan Raiola. Anthony Colandrea has been exactly that. After stops at Virginia and UNLV, Colandrea settled in at Nebraska, throwing for more than 1,100 yards while ranking second among Big Ten quarterbacks in rushing. He possesses the dual threat ability that gives opposing defenses fits. A win would give Nebraska coach Matt Rhule the statement victory he’s been searching for in Lincoln. articles.title: Vida (y deporte) de Muñagorri: "Yo corro enseñando mis cicatrices"
articles.standfirst: Víctima de ETA a los 10 años, protagonista de un libro ahora, Alberto hizo la rehabilitación con los guantes de Arconada para apoyarse después en el ciclismo o las carreras populares
articles.summary: Víctima de ETA a los 10 años, protagonista de un libro ahora, Alberto hizo la rehabilitación con los guantes de Arconada para apoyarse después en el ciclismo o las carreras populares
articles.body: Hamilton regateó a Tendillo en la banda derecha y centró al área pequeña, donde no había ningún compañero suyo. Arconada se tiró a por el balón, lo palmeó y lo dejó botando hacia el punto de penalti, donde Armstrong [...], sorprendido por el regalo, soltó un derechazo al fondo de las redes. Gol de Irlanda del Norte”. José Alberto Muñagorri Berdasco se fue a la cama disgustado aquella noche, después de que, según recogen las primeras líneas del libro en cuestión, cayera en el último partido de la primera fase del Mundial 82 esa España en la que jugaban varios de sus ídolos: Arconada, López Ufarte, Satrústegui o un Zamora que además era paisano de Rentería. Al acostarse era un niño de diez años con una infancia feliz y, sobre todo, con dos piernas y dos ojos, que no hubiera podido imaginar el motivo de la visita que esos mismos futbolistas le rendirían en pocos días. A esas horas alguien había dejado una mochila cargada de explosivos en la plaza Aralar, a 200 metros apenas del domicilio de la familia. Desarrollada por el libro ‘La mochila. Vida de Muñagorri’, escrito por Ander Izagirre (‘Subcampeón’ o ‘Cómo ganar el Giro bebiendo sangre de buey’, sólo atendiendo al deporte) y presentado este martes en Madrid, como hace unos días se había presentado en la propia Rentería, la de Alberto es una historia absolutamente estremecedora. Y lo es desde el momento en que aquella bomba, en principio dirigida contra un local de Iberduero, sobre cuya existencia se había avisado y a la que no se atendió debidamente, terminó llevándose por delante al pequeño. La explosión provocó gravísimas secuelas, incluidas la amputación de la pierna izquierda y la pérdida de visión total de un ojo. Muchos niños vascos, a partir de ahí, crecieron con su nombre grabado como una advertencia: ‘no toques’. Desde entonces, una vida por delante. Y el deporte casi siempre (los guantes regalados por Arconada le acompañaron durante un doloroso proceso de rehabilitación), pero sobre todo cuando peor dadas vinieron, cuando la noche y el speed hicieron de las suyas con Alberto igual que hacían de las suyas con tantos jóvenes que no eran ‘el de la bomba’. Porque Muñagorri no se marchó: siguió en aquella Rentería conflictiva de la que pueden extraerse episodios como el de la madre regresando a casa después de dejar a su hijo en la UCI y encontrándose de frente con una manifestación al grito de '¡Gora ETA!’”. El ciclismo, por ejemplo, porque precisamente Iberduero le regaló una bicicleta de carreras y porque, si el primer paso fue montar sin caerse, el segundo consistió en subir Jaizkibel, casi nada al aparato: “Un día me adelantaron Hermans y Nijboer [ciclistas profesionales neerlandeses]. Vieron la pierna ortopédica y se quedaron a mi lado, hablándome y animándome hasta la cumbre. Me hizo una ilusión de la leche”. El libro, más allá de seguir a Muñagorri, reflexiona también sobre los mecanismos de la violencia, sobre la memoria, sobre el perdón y sobre la convivencia. Y por ahí otra escena deportiva, ésta referida a las carreras populares: “Era el domingo de la Behobia-San Sebastián [...] Completó la prueba en una hora y 48 minutos, segundo en la clasificación de atletas a pie con discapacidad motriz; incluso terminó fresco, sin forzar, porque no quería arriesgarse a sufrir otra lesión y el tiempo era lo de menos. Lo de más fue el paso por Rentería [...] Después de un silencio de décadas, la carrera sirvió para que cientos le dedicaran una ovación de un kilómetro, para que expresaran ese cariño contenido demasiado tiempo”. “Crucé el pueblo llorando, porque soy un llorica”, aseguraba este martes Muñagorri. Quizás para demostrarlo, un par de minutos después derramaba lágrimas conmovido mientras recibía la impresionante ovación que cerraba el acto.

articles.title: Ronaldo apologizes for Portugal walkout; says Jesus broke promise
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo accuses Portugal coach Jorge Jesus of broken promises, but leaves international return open.
articles.body:
Cristiano Ronaldo has accused Portugal ‌coach Jorge Jesus of twice breaking his word, saying a failed agreement to publicly ⁠explain his omission ⁠against Norway drove him out of the camp, but insisting he remained available after any punishment.

In a lengthy statement, the 41-year-old gave his account of the dispute ⁠that prompted his departure from Copenhagen before Portugal’s Nations League match versus Denmark last week.

Ronaldo said Jesus had agreed a plan under which the forward would miss the Norway and Denmark ⁠matches to manage his fitness. However, on the day of the Norway game, the coach told him he would play for 30 minutes.

“Everyone knows the rest. I warmed up from halftime onwards, watched the minutes tick by and wasn’t called on,” Ronaldo said.

“The manager had broken his word to me.”

Portugal’s ‌captain and all-time leading scorer said a subsequent meeting with Jesus, attended by his club side Al Nassr’s sporting director Simao Coutinho, produced an agreement for the coach to clarify events at his next news conference.

According to Ronaldo, an eight-point document was prepared saying he had never demanded playing time, had respected Jesus’s decisions and that the coach asking him to warm up without bringing him on had been a mistake.

Ronaldo said the agreed notes did ⁠not require Jesus to apologise to him but said the coach’s ⁠public remarks bore no resemblance to their private discussion.

“It was the second time he had broken his word to me,” Ronaldo said. “I decided to leave the training camp without waiting for any further broken promises.”

The statement provided Ronaldo’s account⁠, but on Sunday, after Portugal’s win over Norway , Jesus denied he had made any agreement with the player, nevertheless leaving the door open ⁠for his return.

The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) did not immediately respond ⁠to a request for comment about Ronaldo’s statement.

Ronaldo apologised for failing to greet supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates , accepting that his captaincy made his conduct more serious.

“The consequences of my actions must be assessed ‌and punished by the Portuguese Football Federation,” he said.

Despite the rupture, Ronaldo said he was not limiting his international ambitions to a farewell appearance.

“If I’m physically fit, playing for my club – scoring ‌goals, ‌I hope – after serving whatever suspension is imposed on me, I’ll be available, as I’ve always been until now, to compete and win for our national team,” he added.

articles.title: Le lanza la pelota fuera de la pista y gana el punto: la regla de pádel que pocos conocen
articles.standfirst: Durante el P2 de Rotterdam se dio una curiosa acción que ha despertado desconcierto entre los aficionados
articles.summary: Durante el P2 de Rotterdam se dio una curiosa acción que ha despertado desconcierto entre los aficionados
articles.body: En el partido de dieciseisavos de final del P2 de Rotterdam entre Jairo Bautista y Lucas Bergamini contra Dani Santigosa y Álvaro Montiel hubo una jugada muy llamativa. El revés malagueño recuperó un remate, la sacó por la puerta y con la inercia se fue también de la pista. Santigosa corrió y golpeó la pelota directamente contra Bautista: ¿de quién es el punto? Con el reglamento en mano, es para Santigosa, pero esto no siempre ha sido así en el pádel profesional. Esta acción tuvo lugar en uno de los primeros juegos del partido y, como en el pasado la norma no era de esta manera, ha causado cierto desconcierto. Sin embargo, el árbitro acertó con su decisión al darle el punto a Montiel y Santigosa, que estuvo muy rápido e ingenioso para salir de una situación en la que solo tenía esa salida. Cualquier pelota que impacte en el cuerpo es punto para el rival. Sin embargo, durante la etapa de World Padel Tour hubo una acción que cambió esta normativa y que puso una excepción muy concreta para ciertos casos. En el año 2017 tuvo lugar un partido entre Fernando Belasteguín y Pablo Lima contra Fede Chingotto y Juan Tello. El ‘Boss’ remató, el de Olavarría corrió, llegó y, al igual que Bautista, con la inercia se fue de la pista por la puerta para no tocar la red. Bela, al que le quedó la pelota en una posición muy incómoda, tiró contra el ‘Ratón’ y se anotó el punto. Aquella pillería del revés argentino hizo que se reformulara la norma. Con el objetivo de que no se repitiera algo así, donde un jugador le tira al otro al cuerpo porque no tiene otra opción, se dictó que en este tipo de acciones sería punto para el que recibe el pelotazo en caso de que el golpe no vaya en dirección a la pista. De hecho, años después ocurrió algo similar entre Lebrón y Ramiro Moyano, pero, con la norma ya cambiada, el punto subió para el gaditano, ya que fue el argentino quien intentó emular aquel ingenioso golpe del ‘Boss’. No obstante, años después se ha vuelto a dar esta situación, pero con otro final. El punto fue para Santigosa y mucha gente ha pensado que el árbitro se había equivocado… pero no. Esta modificación tuvo lugar solamente en World Padel Tour. La FIP nunca llegó a adoptarla y siempre ha sido válido aplicar esta picardía en sus torneos. Así figura en el Manual de Protocolo y Actuación Arbitral de la Federación, que es la normativa del circuito Premier Padel. Esta norma dice: “Durante el punto, un jugador tiene permitido dirigir la bola hacia el cuerpo de un oponente, ya sea dentro o fuera de la pista con juego exterior”. Por tanto, Gustavo Cueto, juez de silla de este encuentro, hizo una correcta interpretación del reglamento al darle por válida esta jugada a Dani Santigosa. Al final, Montiel y el madrileño se llevaron el triunfo, pasando de ser 'lucky losers' a meterse en los octavos de final de este P2 de Dusseldorf tras ganar a Jairo Bautista y Lucas Bergamini por 7-5 y 7-6.

La jugada de Santigosa con Jairo Bautista.

articles.title: Ohio State Legend Urban Meyer: Michigan Is A 'Train Wreck'
articles.summary: Ohio State Buckeyes coaching legend Urban Meyer called the Michigan Wolverines a "train wreck."
articles.body: A train wreck is defined as "a violent and destructive crash involving a train" or "an utter disaster or mess." But for Urban Meyer, that's just the 2026 Michigan Wolverines. "I don't see a fast solution at all, because I have not said this yet, it's a train wreck right now," Meyer said about the Wolverines on the latest episode of "The Triple Option." "I stood right there and watched it [on the sideline against Minnesota] … This is not all on [quarterback Bryce Underwood]. Unfortunately, he plays that position that is all on him. You know, whenever they win, the quarterback gets too much glory, and when they lose, they get too much blame. But that sideline, I just didn't feel the dudes anywhere. And I was looking. I was staring. You know, plays are going on, and I'm staring because I did that for so long. I'm saying, 'Where are the grown-a-- men?' "And I didn't feel it. I didn't see it when there had to be a big stop. I didn't see the energy, and I just didn't see it … passion, energy and toughness. I didn't see it." Michigan is coming off a Week 5 loss on the road to the Minnesota Golden Gophers, which marked their first win at home over the Wolverines since 1977; it was the site of FOX's "Big Noon Kickoff." This defeat for Michigan came one week after it lost at home to the Iowa Hawkeyes on a walk-off, 16-yard touchdown pass. And, of course, the Wolverines beat the Western Michigan Broncos at home in Week 1 on a 47-yard, Hail Mary pass, which came after one second was controversially placed back on the clock. The Wolverines, who are in their first season with former Utah Utes coach Kyle Whittingham as their head coach, are 3-2 and unranked. Michigan's Offensive Struggles Michigan's offense is last in the Big Ten in passing yards (180.8 per game), 17th in the 18-team conference in both total yards (315.8 per game) and points (23.0 per game) and 13th in rushing yards (135.0 per game). Underwood, who's in his second season under center for Michigan, has totaled 881 passing yards, five passing touchdowns, four interceptions and a 132.3 passer rating, while completing 59.3% of his passes. He has also rushed for 212 yards and two touchdowns. Of Underwood's mere 67 completions, 49 of them have gone to wide receivers JJ Buchanan (24 receptions for 446 yards and four scores) and Andrew Marsh (25 receptions for 268 yards and one score). Meanwhile, Michigan's defense has been among the elite in the sport, as the Wolverines are second in the Big Ten in both opponent yards (241.4 per game) and opponent passing yards (146.8 per game), fourth in opponent rushing yards (94.6 per game) and fifth in opponent points (15.8 per game). Senior linebacker Troy Bowles has a team-high 40 combined tackles, while defensive end and fellow senior John Henry Daley has three of the Wolverines' 12 sacks. Michigan's Schedule Following a Week 6 bye, Michigan hosts the Penn State Nittany Lions on Oct. 17. Of its seven remaining games, Michigan has four ranked opponents: No. 7 Indiana, No. 13 Oregon, No. 21 UCLA and No. 5 Ohio State. As for the bearer of bad news for Michigan, the Buckeyes went 7-0 against the Wolverines with Meyer, who's now a College Football Studio Analyst for FOX's "Big Noon Kickoff," as their head coach from 2012-18, a stint highlighted by Ohio State winning the national championship in the 2014 college football season. Catch Meyer and the "Big Noon Kickoff" crew in Lincoln, Nebraska this coming Saturday, as the Nebraska Cornhuskers host Indiana (12 p.m. ET on FOX).

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo Is Not Retiring, Blames Coach Jorge Jesus For Portugal Walkout
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is not following Lionel Messi into international retirement just yet.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo is not following Lionel Messi into international retirement just yet. The Portugal superstar said he will remain available to play for his national team, despite having walked out on the squad during the current international window. In a long statement issued through the Portuguese media Tuesday, Ronaldo said recently hired coach Jorge Jesus had not been true to his word about when he would play the striker in the latest round of Nations League matches. Still, the 41-year-old Ronaldo said he owed his teammates an apology and expects to receive a punishment. "I can promise all my fans, and naturally especially all Portuguese people, that we will have one or more farewell matches. There will be time for that," Ronaldo said. He added: "Therefore, if I am physically fit, playing for my club, hopefully scoring goals, then after serving whatever suspension is imposed on me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team." Ronaldo said he had agreed to a plan for managing his playing time and that he expected the coach to publicly clarify the situation and accept responsibility. He said Jesus did not follow through and instead spoke aggressively at a press conference, causing a breakdown of trust. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Justin Herbert, Kirk Cousins, and 2 Other Must-Sit Fantasy Football Week 5 Quarterbacks

articles.body:
It has been a sorrowful season for those who drafted Bo Nix and Justin Herbert. Prior to Week 4, Drake Maye owners could have said the same. As I always say, no week is the same as the last. Things can change on a whim. But data can also be interpreted at will, and the four quarterbacks below are suggested sits in Week 5.

Completion Percentage data is from PFF.com Offensive EPA Stats are from NFLverse Defensive EPA Stats are from draftwithdoug.com

Nix has only met QB1 status once this season: in Week 3, he was QB6 overall. This season, Nix is the QB19 in fantasy football. He cannot be trusted at his current output. Nix is only 18th in Adjusted Completion Percentage and 27th in EPA per Dropback.

According to Sleeper, Nix is being started in 35% of fantasy leagues. It is time for change. Nix once had value as a runner, but to date, He has 25 rushing yards on 14 attempts.

No quarterback with at least 100 dropbacks this season is worse than Herbert in PFF Passing Grade. The Mike McDaniel system isn't pleasing the young signal caller, as he ranks 23rd in Adjusted Completion Percentage and 28th in EPA per Dropback.

To make things worse, Ladd McConkey is likely to be out this Sunday . Nothing has been seen in Los Angeles. Nothing makes Herbert a confident play, with zero wins and four losses.

Love's season has been solid at QB15. Not quite a ceiling met for Love, but it is okay. He is averaging 260 yards per game on 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. Yet, the output is not quite at a level of football worth shooing in at his weekly start.

The Packers face their division rival, the Chicago Bears, this weekend. This past Sunday, they held the Jets to single-digit completions. This season, the Bears are 2nd in Defensive Pass EPA Allowed per Play and are top-10 in fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks.

Expect Cousins to Normalize in October. He is the QB9 in fantasy football. Yet, once you factor in power ratings, matchups, expected pass rates, and more, Cousins won't be in my top-20 quarterbacks for Week 5.

Cousins lacks any rushing ability. He must pass for at least 250 yards and 2+ touchdowns to be worth it. He cannot be relied upon to do that weekly on an offense implied to score around 20 points per game, according to ESPN's FPI.

articles.title: Lane Johnson retires with a compelling Hall of Fame résumé
articles.summary: Lane Johnson’s combination of championships, individual honors and sustained dominance gives the retiring Eagles tackle a powerful Pro Football Hall of Fame...
articles.body:
Lane Johnson's playing career is over. The debate over his place in NFL history shouldn't be complicated.

Johnson retires with two Super Bowl championships, three NFC titles, six Pro Bowl selections, and five Associated Press All-Pro honors. He was a first-team All-Pro twice and remained among the league's best right tackles well into his 30s. Those honors provide the foundation of Johnson's Pro Football Hall of Fame case. The film strengthens it.

At his peak, Johnson combined uncommon athleticism with the strength and technical control required to neutralize elite pass rushers. Philadelphia trusted him in isolated protection situations, allowing the offense to allocate help elsewhere. His ability to handle those assignments shaped what the Eagles could call.

Johnson also performed at a championship level across different coaching staffs, schemes, and quarterback situations. He helped Philadelphia win Super Bowl LII following the 2017 season and Super Bowl LIX seven years later.

The longevity between those titles is significant. Johnson was not merely a remaining veteran on the second championship roster. He was still one of the league's best players at his position today when he announced his decision. He allowed no sacks during the 2024 regular season while helping clear the way for Saquon Barkley's 2,005 rushing yards.

Right tackles have historically received less recognition than players protecting a quarterback's blind side. Modern offenses and modern pass rushers have weakened that distinction. Defenses move their premier rushers across the formation, making high-level tackle play essential on both sides. Johnson met that challenge for more than a decade. His résumé includes the honors, team success, longevity, and dominant peak expected of a Hall of Fame offensive lineman.

His next football honor should be induction in Canton five years from now.

articles.title: Rangers CHL, USHL prospects notebook: Strong starts for Anderson, Farhammar
articles.summary: The third week of play in North America’s major junior leagues provided a good look at how the Rangers prospects […]
articles.body:
The third week of play in North America's major junior leagues provided a good look at how the Rangers prospects are settling into their seasons. Some players are finding early momentum, others are adjusting to new leagues and a few are already standing out with strong performances.

This past week had a mix of everything, but here are the two prospects who made the biggest impact in Week 3.

First Star: Darian Anderson — Flint Firebirds (OHL)

Darian Anderson , New York's sixth-round pick (No. 163 overall) put together another strong weekend for Flint and took the lead in scoring among Rangers' junior prospects.

He scored his fourth goal of the season on Saturday, but the Firebirds lost 3-2 to the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds. Anderson opened the scoring at 10:01 of the first period when he slipped a shot through the goalie's five‑hole.

Sunday's game against London was a different story. Anderson earned Second Star honors with a goal and two assists in a 7-2 win against London. His shot from the high slot created a rebound that turned into the Firebirds' first goal. Anderson then scored his fifth of the season during a power-play scramble, giving Flint a 3-0 lead. That turned out to be his second game-winning goal of the season and his second on the power play.

🚨: Darian Anderson 🍏: Jimmy Lombardi 🍏: Martins Klaucans pic.twitter.com/yzKQUDCawD — Flint Firebirds (@FlintFirebirds) October 4, 2026

🚨: Darian Anderson 🍏: Jimmy Lombardi 🍏: Martins Klaucans pic.twitter.com/yzKQUDCawD

Flint Firebirds (@FlintFirebirds) October 4, 2026

He added another assist in the third period when his shot was deflected into the net for Flint's sixth goal. Anderson leads Flint with five goals and is second with seven points in five games.

Only five players scored more goals so far in the OHL , and each played more games than Anderson.

Second Star: Felix Farhammar — Muskegon Lumberjacks (USHL)

Felix Farhammar , a defenseman who was New York's seventh-round pick (No. 203 overall) in 2025, continues to adapt to North American hockey at both ends of the ice.

He scored his second goal of the season on Friday, when Muskegon doubled up the Madison Capitols 6-3, then stretched his points streak to five games on Saturday with the primary assist on the game's first goal. It gave Muskegon an early lead in a game the Lumberjacks lost 4-3 in a shootout to Madison.

Farhammar has two goals and five points in six games, a nice way to start his USHL season. He's adjusting well to the league's pace and physical style.

Danai Shaiikov — Gatineau Olympiques (QMJHL)

Goaltender Danai Shaiikov stopped 24 of 26 shots, when Gatineau rallied from a 2-0 deficit to defeat Shawinigan 3-2 in overtime on Friday night. He allowed one goal, a short-handed tally, on 10 shots in the first period and was beaten through a screen in the second, but stopped all five shots he faced in the third period and four more in overtime for the win.

The Rangers' third-round pick (No. 67) in the 2026 NHL draft was back in the net Saturday at Val‑d'Or and opened strong, stopping eight of nine shots in the first period against the Foreurs. He stopped all 11 shots he faced in the second period. But he allowed the game-tying goal early in the third and surrendered the game-winner in overtime. Shaiikov finished with 25 saves in the 3-2 loss.

He did not play Sunday, dressing as the backup in Gatineau's 5–4 win.

Shaiikov is 3-0-2 record, a. 2.64 goals-against average (tied for sixth best in the QMJHL ), and a save percentage of .895.

Spencer Bowes scored his third goal of the season, an empty‑netter, to cap Ottawa's 4-1 win over Oshawa on Friday. He finished with one goal on five shots and was 9 of 18 on face-offs.

He scored the 67s' final goal of the game Saturday in a 6-1 win over Erie, finishing with one goal, three shots on goal and was plus-2. He took a roughing minor and won six of 17 face-offs.
