articles.title: Dan Campbell gets passionate about offense ‘mediocrity,’ defensive fixes
articles.summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell gave a passionate radio interview about the offense and defense struggles.
articles.body:
You could hear the passion in Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell's voice on Tuesday morning as he faced another barrage of questions about the team's lackluster start to the season—this time courtesy of John Jansen and Jim Costa, the hosts of 97.1 The Ticket's morning show. As the interview progressed, Campbell got more and more passionate with his answers, even admitting at the end of the interview that, "I am fired up, man. I am. I'm going forward, not backward."

Here's a breakdown of the biggest takeaways from Campbell radio appearance.

He's not accepting mediocrity from the offense

Campbell has received a bit of criticism for continuing to point to the offense needing to be better, when the Lions defense is arguably the worst in the league. On Tuesday, Campbell set the record straight, noting that the offense is too talented to accept what has been a relatively mediocre performance. When asked if the defense is putting too much pressure on the offense to be perfect, here was Campbell's emphatic response

"If you want to be great, they should want to score 35 points a game at a minimum. That's what greatness is. That's what they're charged with. We've got plenty of weapons on offense, and if we're going to accept mediocrity, then no. Then yeah, we can make all of the excuses in the world. But if we want to spit and sputter and be average, that's one thing. "We're not going to be average. We're going to raise the floor on these guys. Man, we're going to push them. "We've got too much offensively right now. Our quarterback's too good. Our playmakers are too good. And we've got a young, hungry offensive line that's got a ton of room to grow."

"If you want to be great, they should want to score 35 points a game at a minimum. That's what greatness is. That's what they're charged with. We've got plenty of weapons on offense, and if we're going to accept mediocrity, then no. Then yeah, we can make all of the excuses in the world. But if we want to spit and sputter and be average, that's one thing.

"We're not going to be average. We're going to raise the floor on these guys. Man, we're going to push them.

"We've got too much offensively right now. Our quarterback's too good. Our playmakers are too good. And we've got a young, hungry offensive line that's got a ton of room to grow."

While the offense ranks in the top-10 or top-five in many stats, there are some significant areas to improve that could be described as average. In the running game, they're just 16th in yards per rush (4.2) and 17th in rush EPA. They are also just 14th in third-down conversion rate (39.1%), and they've gone three-and-out t-17th most .

Jansen led off the interview asking Campbell if he could pick one thing for the defense to improve upon this week; what would it be? Campbell's answer was a familiar one:

"I want our guys to be where they're supposed to be when they're supposed to be there. We need to be on point. Our discipline has got to clean up," Campbell said.

This matches almost verbatim what Campbell said after Detroit's loss against the Bills in Week 2.

"Be where you're supposed to be when you're supposed to be there and do it with urgency across the board," Campbell said after the Bills game.

As to what is causing players to be out of place, Campbell listed a few things. For one, players are compensating for other players' mistakes. Then, he believes the Lions are getting undisciplined with their eyes.

"Probably boot(legs), dirty eyes on some stuff," Campbell said. "The slam boots, the overs. That's where we're getting in trouble a little bit. It's not really man or match coverage."

Ultimately, Campbell believes that despite the coverage issues, they have capable players in the building.

"Inevitably, somebody's going to be locked up one-on-one with no help, and you've got to win. And we have the guys that can win," Campbell said.

Looking for someone on defense to step up vs. tight ends

We talked last week about the Lions' struggles against tight ends . With one of the best tight ends in Trey McBride on deck for Cardinals week, the radio hosts asked Campbell how they plan to prepare. He gave a pretty unique answer:

"You know what I want? I want somebody to come in tomorrow and say, 'I want McBride.' That's what I want," Campbell said. "I want to know who that's going to be on our defense."

When asked who he'd prefer that player to be, he answered, "Anybody."

Campbell noted that he certainly understands all the criticism of Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard given the results and the statistics. But he backed Sheppard full-throatedly.

"I believe in Kelvin Sheppard, and I believe we've got a lot of meat on the bone with this defense right now. Like I said, we're going to continue to tweak. We've got more things that we can do with what we have here. There's different calls, we've got to be more disciplined, and then we're going to get some guys more opportunities to play here. We're going to find the right recipe. "Here's what I do know: At crunch time in that game the other day, at the end of the game with our defense on the field, we got two critical stops. That's what I do know. So at the end of the day, after all of that, we had a chance to win that game and we couldn't close it out. So I'll take that."

Scotland took the lead at Hampden Park after 31 minutes when Ryan Christie finished from close range, turning in Oliver McBurnie's assist following a set-piece situation. The hosts had slightly more of the ball and looked well placed after the opener, but the contest was already becoming increasingly untidy.

The match changed colour before half-time when John McGinn was shown a red card for Scotland on 44 minutes, and Slovenia were also reduced to 10 men early in the second half after David Zec's dismissal. Even so, the visitors found an equaliser on 56 minutes, as Aljosa Matko curled in a left-footed effort from outside the box, with Danijel Sturm providing the assist.

Scotland's problems deepened on 68 minutes when Luis Binks was sent off, leaving them unable to sustain control in a game that remained finely balanced. Slovenia then made their advantage count on 71 minutes, with Sturm scoring from the centre of the box after being set up by Matko to complete the turnaround.

The statistics reflected a close contest: Scotland finished with 52% possession, nine shots and four on target, while Slovenia posted 10 shots, four corners and an expected goals figure of 1.26. articles.title: Iowa football injury update: DB Tyler Brown 'out for a while'
articles.summary: Iowa head football coach Kirk Ferentz said that defensive back Tyler Brown remains "out for a while."
articles.body:
Iowa head football coach Kirk Ferentz said in his Tuesday press conference that defensive back Tyler Brown remains sidelined.

"Tyler's out. I don't know if I said whenever it was, last week or two weeks ago, but he's going to be out for a while," Ferentz said.

Brown missed a considerable amount of fall camp and the first two weeks of the season as he dealt with a muscle strain .

The 5-foot-10, 201-pound defensive back did play against both Northern Iowa and Michigan , but Brown appeared to be limping toward the end of Iowa's 20-19 win over the Wolverines . That created a concern that he might have reaggravated his muscle strain.

Ferentz tabbed Brown as questionable in his press remarks last week ahead of Iowa's matchup against Ohio State . Then, the James Madison transfer and Annapolis, Md., native was ruled out on the Hawkeyes' availability report prior to its game against the Buckeyes.

Brown has registered 11 tackles and one forced fumble so far this season.

Fellow safety and Iowa team captain Zach Lutmer exited Iowa's loss against Ohio State . Afterwards, Ferentz said he thought it was cramping for Lutmer. Ferentz confirmed on Tuesday that Lutmer will be available on Friday as No. 18 Iowa travels to Washington (3-2, 0-2 Big Ten).

However, Ferentz said he doesn't think Ty Hudkins will be available for the Hawkeyes on Friday night.

"I don't think we can count on Hudkins based on what I know thus far for this week," Ferentz said.

That sets Iowa up where Lutmer, Anthony Hawkins and Xavier Styles figure to be the three primary options at safety against the Huskies. Ferentz said Marcello Vitti could also factor in.

"Basically, that's your three top guys are right there, and maybe get (Marcello) Vitti or some other people to work into it. Hopefully we keep the guys out there and keep healthy and just keep improving, especially in the communication part. It's funny. Micah Hyde, that was the first point he made when he spoke to the team on Friday.

"We did have some communication issues. Part of that was crowd noise here. Home crowd noise can be a factor for the defense, and so we've just got to make sure everybody is on the same page. We won't have that problem for them this week. I guess that's good news," Ferentz said.

Kickoff between Iowa and Washington is set for 8 p.m. CT on Friday night. The game will be broadcast on either Fox or FS1.

articles.title: Croatia 1-2 Spain: Mikel Merino the hero as La Roja advance to Nations League quarter-finals
articles.summary: The champs stay undefeated
articles.body:
Reigning world champions Spain have extended their historic unbeaten record to 42 matches and have also clinched an early spot in the Nations League quarter-finals thanks to a 2-1 comeback win away to Croatia on Tuesday night.

Rodri, Pedri, Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo and Pau Cubarsí represented Barcelona in the starting lineup and Fermín López came off the bench, but the hero of the night was another substitute as Mikel Merino scored both goals and sealed another victory for La Roja .

After a horrible loss to England at the weekend, Croatia were determined to play a more solid and physical game against the world champions, and were the better team throughout the half with the way they competed defensively and brought danger on the counter.

Spain didn't help themselves and made a lot of silly mistakes in the buildup, and one of them led to a counter-attack that ended with a header by Ivan Perisic to give the hosts the lead. Croatia had a couple of other big chances thanks to Spain mistakes, and Unai Simón needed to make some important saves to avoid a two-goal deficit.

La Roja tried to react and dominated the ball without creating a true chance until the final play of the half, when Pedri found Lamine Yamal with an amazing through ball and the teenager tried to find the near post but hit the side netting instead.

Spain were behind at halftime and needing to play better with the ball, while Croatia looked to remain physical, passionate and intense to defend their lead in the second half.

Luis de la Fuente sent on his favorite super sub at halftime as Mikel Merino came on, and Spain also upped their urgency and started to create real danger with Yamal at the heart of the action.

Dani Olmo also became more influential, and it was his assist that set up Merino's equalizer at the hour mark. Croatia did a very good job of defending and mostly frustrated the Spanish attempts at a winner, but Perisic was sent off for a second yellow card and Croatia couldn't hang on for much longer.

Rodri, Pedri, Olmo and Yamal all came off in the second half but Fermín López was on the pitch and had a front row seat as he watched Merino receive a nice pass from Martín Zubimendi inside the box and fire a rocket into the roof of the net to complete the comeback at the death.

The final whsitle came to extend Spain's historic unbeaten record and keep them all alone in first place in the group while also booking an early spot in the Nations League quarter-finals.

La Roja 's international window ends without any injuries for Barça players and with four good wins. Pretty good work from the world champs.

His team won the league rather unexpectedly, and a major part of that was the coup of signing N'Golo Kante in the summer when he arrived. Conte says it almost didn't happen.

"We hadn't made any big signings. We signed David Luiz, Marcos Alonso and Kante — the club asked me 10 times if I was sure about him. He wasn't the typical Chelsea player: tall and handsome. Because of how successful he ended up being, it's easy to forget there were indeed doubts about Kante's move to Chelsea. articles.title: Is there cause for concern with Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt?
articles.summary: Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt has averaged just 2.8 yards per carry so far this season
articles.body:
The commitment to it is fine. Offensive coordinator David Blough continues to call for runs at an appropriate rate. The numbers look just sort of okay.

You take away the quarterback runs, though, and an eybrow gets raised.

We aren't talking about a nuclear winter, here. We're just making folks aware that the bedrock of this offensive system isn't hitting on all cylinders. The bottom line stats, as we've mentioned, can also be skewed by mobile quarterbacks.

Here's what we're trying to get to, in this long introduction: the curious case of Jacory Croskey-Merritt, who is averaging less than four yards per carry over four games. That number dropped to less than two over the last two games, with Rachaad White unavailable on Sunday against the Colts.

The prevailing theory was that Croskey-Merritt would fit well with Blough's rushing scheme, which is predicated on outside zone runs. That hasn't been the case to this point.

Look, I'll just put this out there. I'm not a "tape guy" and I'm not going to pretend to be one. We have Mark Tyler and Jamual Forrest and John Portis for that stuff. But I have been around the game for a super long time and can analyze the numbers and the advanced metrics. And, frankly, I know a good player when I see one. I covered LaDainian Tomlinson for goodness sakes, so I have a gold standard. It also doesn't take a rocket scientist to see that the Commanders aren't efficient running the football at important times.

Croskey-Merritt's explosiveness might be his best feature, as we saw several times last year. So is his decisiveness and burst into the second level. Outside a play negated by penalty, we haven't seen that this season.

He's still in prove-it mode, considering it's just his second season. But…the fact we saw Rachaad White average 4.4 yards per carry vs. Seattle to Croskey-Merritt's 1.9 isn't great. Neither is the fact that Austin Ekeler has now joined the roster, and was efficient with his opportunities.

Is it the back or is it the system or the line and the operation? Evaluate that in the article comments below. But it's fair to wonder how long the Commanders stick with Croskey-Merritt and whether this is a temporary issue or a major cause for concern. I bring this all up for a discussion point, as the Commanders head into a now vital Week 5 contest with the New York Giants.

Is it time to pivot higher carry counts towards Ekeler or White? Or am I overreacting? Let's discuss.

articles.title: McDonald’s Is Handing out Pickle Juice Shots to Chicago Marathon Runners (and Fans): Where to Get Yours
articles.summary: Fans can also get the limited-edition pickle shots at select McDonald’s locations throughout the city on Oct. 11 between 7 a.m. and 3 p.m. CT
articles.body:
McDonald's is handing out free pickle juice shots for runners and fans during the Chicago Marathon

Five pit stops along the route will offer two free bottles per person, and select Chicago locations will offer the limited-edition brine from 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. on race day

The chain cites electrolytes and cramp management as the reasoning behind handing out the liquid

McDonald's is offering Chicago Marathon runners a pickle power-up.

The fast-food chain announced that it is bottling its pickle juice and handing it out at various points throughout the Chicago Marathon on Sunday, Oct. 11, as well as throughout the weekend, according to a press release shared with PEOPLE.

Two free bottles each of the "limited-edition pickle brine shots" will be handed out to both runners and spectators at the following Pickle Boost Pit Stops during the marathon:

The locations are placed along the race route at miles 2, 3, 9, 11 and 23.

Fans can also get the pickle shots at select McDonald's locations throughout the city on Oct. 11 between 7 a.m. and 3 p.m. CT.

McDonald's will also give out the pickle juice at its Pickle Boost Preview on Friday, Oct. 9 from 7 a.m. to 1 p.m. CT.

The pickle juice pop-up will take place at 2401 N Lake Shore Drive, along the Lakefront Trail, a popular running path that the brand says will be the site of plenty of shakeout runs.

"Fans can get a first taste and early access to race day MVP," the release said.

The chain cited pickle juice's electrolytes and how it helps athletes manage cramps during workouts as the reasoning behind the promotion.

Per BBC , the briny liquid is a staple among athletes, who drink it during exercise to reduce cramping because it contains electrolytes like sodium and potassium and triggers a mouth reflex that signals muscles to stop cramping.

"McDonald's fans always go the extra mile for our pickles, and – in honor of marathon season – we're going 26.2 for you," McDonald's said in its release. "We're bottling up the salty, athlete-ready brine from the beloved ingredient for one of the biggest marathon weekends in the country in Chicago."

McDonald's recently brought back its Monopoly game .

From Oct. 6 to Nov. 1, rewards members can peel game pieces from Monopoly menu items and scan them into the chain's app for free food and loyalty points or the chance to win prizes.

"MONOPOLY at McDonald's is more than just a game. It's about childhood memories, family moments and surprises that make our day," a spokesperson for McDonald's said in a release.

The game returned in 2025 after a nine-year hiatus.

Launched in 1987, it faced some scandals in its early years.

When the promotion began, Jerome "Jerry" Jacobson, the security director for the marketing company that initiated the game, stole game pieces and gave them to people for a cut, per The New York Times .

He later admitted to defrauding the game of $24 million in cash and prizes and was forced to pay $12.5 million in restitution and was sentenced to 37 months in prison.

articles.title: Tyreek Hill civil trial: Ex-wife accusses WR of trying to punch her in stomach while pregnant
articles.summary: Star NFL wide receiver Tyreek Hill, currently a free agent, is reportedly on the cusp of returning to the league after a knee injury ended his season with th...
articles.body:
Star NFL wide receiver Tyreek Hill, currently a free agent, is reportedly on the cusp of returning to the league after a knee injury ended his season with the Miami Dolphins last year.

Hill has been heavily linked to the Kansas City Chiefs, the franchise he started his career with, following a pair of injuries to the Chiefs' top two wide receivers in Week 4. However, Hill's return to the league has been complicated by off-the-field issues, which could warrant punishment from the league .

Hill is currently under an active Personal Conduct Policy review stemming from allegations of domestic violence made by his ex-wife, Keeta Vaccaro. As Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio has noted, Hill's colored history could impact any punishment from the league for Vaccaro's allegations.

Hill's history complicates the situation. Past incidents, including a 2015 guilty plea to domestic assault and battery by strangulation in an incident involving his then-pregnant girlfriend, could result in an enhanced suspension — if the league finds a Personal Conduct Policy violation in connection with Vaccaro's allegations," Florio wrote.

Hill underwent a civil trial on Tuesday in relation to Hill's allegations, in which Vaccaro accused the wide receiver of "attempting a punch at her stomach while she was pregnant with his child in July 2024," per The Athletic's Jesse Newell.

"During civil trial today, Tyreek Hill's ex-wife Lakeeta Vaccaro Hill accused him of attempting a punch at her stomach while she was pregnant with his child in July 2024. Lakeeta said she put her hands on her stomach to block the strike, which made contact with her hands," Newell posted on X.

"She said Tyreek told her then that he didn't want the baby. Lakeeta described the day as 'probably the worst of all these abuse times.' She also alleged Tyreek pulled her hair and ripped it out the same day."

If Hill is found guilty of Vaccaro's allegations, it's hard to imagine a world in which the NFL does not punish him severely, halting any imminent return to the field.

articles.title: Why Memphis' Charles Huff is only looking forward in 'Battle for the Bones' rivalry
articles.summary: Last season, Memphis football vs. UAB turned into one of the most shocking upsets of the 2025 season. This year, Charles Huff is only looking ahead.
articles.body:
Last season, Memphis football vs. UAB turned into one of the most shocking upsets of the 2025 season.

The Tigers, potentially seven days away from hosting "College GameDay," lost in Birmingham as 23.5-point favorites.

This year, Memphis coach Charles Huff isn't talking about it.

"It's a different culture," he said at his news conference on Oct. 6. "I can't speak to that week, that game, that year."

Memphis' coach for that game was Ryan Silverfield, but he left after the season for Arkansas . He was replaced by Huff, who brought in an almost entirely new roster. Memphis has only a handful of players on the current roster who even played in the game last season, so it hasn't been much of a talking point this week.

Charles Huff, Memphis Tigers football coach in first season

The game, which some Memphis fans consider a rivalry and some fans are adamantly against being called a rivalry, is known as the "Battle for the Bones" and features a 94-pound bronze rack of ribs as a trophy. That trophy has been in Birmingham for the past year after spending more than a decade in Memphis.

"We addressed it in the summer," Huff said. "I think the attachment now is maybe not so much of a bitter rivalry but how much it means to our fans. Our players truly believe if something's important to our fans, then it needs to be important to us. This is one of those things."

Huff said he views the game as a chance for Memphis' players to give back to the fans who care about the game and about winning back the trophy. UAB had been one of the worst teams in the conference for the last few seasons, which led to Trent Dilfer getting fired the week before last year's Memphis vs. UAB game. Alex Mortensen coached his first ever game and Ryder Burton made his first collegiate start at quarterback on that night, and they each looked like stars.

Burton has been solid since then, too. UAB has won two games in a row, including an upset win at home over Navy to open American Conference play.

It sets up an interesting game, even if last year's matchup won't be part of Memphis' preparation.

"I've never lost, so I don't know what it feels like to lose the bones," Huff said. "And I say that not in a boastful way. I don't know, so I can't talk to them about a loss that I wasn't a part of. On the flip side, I've never won it. So I can't talk to them about what it feels like to win it, either."

articles.title: High school football midseason report: Top teams, breakout players, surprise teams
articles.summary: The E-N gathered top teams, breakout players, surprise teams from the first half of the 2026 high school football season.
articles.body:
We've reached the halfway point of the 2026 UIL high school football season. Several teams are living up to their preseason hype, while some other teams - and players - have been a surprise. What will the second half of the season have in store for high school football fans across Texas? And what are the most important games moving forward? Here are our takeaways from the first half of the regular season:

Area's top teams are exactly the ones we thought they would be

The Jaguars, ranked No. 1 in the area and No. 7 in the Class 6A state rankings , are 4-0 (2-0 in District 28-6A). It's tough to measure the Jaguars statistically because they've essentially played 3 ½ games after their opener was canceled and their 37-0 victory against Odessa was stopped at halftime, both because of weather. But, their playmakers - quarterback Elvis Estrada, receivers Braelyn Allen and Bryson Thompson - are leading the way.

Smithson Valley: Entering the season, the Rangers needed to replenish its front seven on defense that was hit hard with graduation. After a 5-0 start, that's happened. Smithson Valley, the state's No. 1 team in Class 5A Division I, has yielded just 45 points. On top of that, the Rangers have been prolific on offense with 350 points. They are 3-0 in district, having topped 70 points each time, including an 84-7 win against Cedar Creek.

Steele: The Knights (3-1-1) are the state's No. 18 ranked team in Class 6A and No. 3 in San Antonio. Steele is currently riding a 31-game district winning streak and has won six league titles in a row. The Knights dropped a road game against then state-ranked Humble Atascocita (38-23) and tied long time nemesis Lake Travis (28-28) when their game was stopped in the second half because of weather. After that, they had decisive wins against Wagner and Pieper in District 27-6A.

Brennan: The Bears (4-1), ranked No. 22 in the state 6A rankings, are in the thick of yet another district championship. That's no surprise to anyone who has followed the Bears since their inception in 2010 with coach Steve Basore. After going 0-10 in their first season, the Bears have qualified for the playoffs each year and have won eight district titles. Brennan has been on a tear since dropping their opener against Austin Vandegrift, 28-21. Since then, the Bears have recorded three shutouts and have allowed 14 points in four games.

Boerne: The UIL realignment gods may have opened the way for the Greyhounds to get to Dallas for the state finals. Boerne, ranked No. 2 in the state, has advanced to the Class 5A Division II state semifinals the last two years only to be stopped by Richmond Randle and running back Landin Williams-Callis, a Texas pledge, each time. Randle is now in 5A Division I while Boerne remains in Division II. The Greyhounds' top playmakers from last year have played a big part in their 5-0 start with quarterback Grant Sweeney, receiver Zach Freasier and running back Callan Combs.

Kenyon and Kyrin Armelin, Kerrville Tivy, juniors, wide receivers: The twin brothers have played a critical role in Tivy's pass-heavy offense, and they've attracted the attention of multiple Power Four college programs this fall. The juniors have earned offers from schools such as Texas A&M, Oklahoma and Houston. Kenyon has already amassed 10 touchdowns and 781 yards, averaging 26 yards per catch. Kyrin has reeled in eight touchdowns passes and piled up 674 yards this season, He is averaging 3.2 yards per catch.

Ryder Flugence, Boerne Champion, sophomore, quarterback: Flugence gained national attention when he was ranked the No. 1 football recruit in his class nationally by 247Sports . In his first year as Boerne Champion's starter, Flugence has thrown 896 yards and 16 touchdowns on 58-of-92 passing. He's also rushed for 543 yards and seven touchdowns across six games. Flugence has also taken a few reps in Champion's secondary.

Jayshawn Mitchell, Brennan, junior, running back: Mitchell is responsible for the bulk of Brennan's rushing yardage this season. While he played for Brennan last year, he's already surpassed his total rushing yardage from last year in six games this season. He's rushed for 742 yards and 17 touchdowns on 72 carries, and Mitchell's recruiting stock has only risen since the season began. He's already earned offers from Georgia and Alabama.

Cohen Stehling, Kerrville Tivy, freshman, quarterback: Stehling had the difficult job of stepping into Tivy's starting quarterback role after the graduation of last year's starter Colin Rose. But he's quickly grown into the role. Tivy is off to a 5-0 start and Stehling has even broken school records along the way . He threw for 515 yards and eight touchdowns in a 70-14 win over Austin LBJ, setting a new program record for most passing yards in a single game. The previous record of 503 yards was set in 2010 by future Heisman winner and Texas A&M quarterback Johnny Manziel.

MacArthur: The Brahmas earned their first ever win under head coach and MacArthur grad Jordon Ricker in their season opener and have been off to their best start in nearly a decade. MacArthur is currently 4-1 and 2-0 in District 14-5A-I . The Brahmas are currently tied for first place in the district with Medina Valley and are in position to make the playoffs for the first time since 2017.

Madison: The Mavericks have already surpassed their win total from last year in Myles Duelm's first year as a head coach . Madison's lone loss from the first half of the season was a 45-43 triple overtime loss to Roosevelt. The Madison defense has impressed so far, posting two shutouts and averaging 17.4 points allowed per game.

Key games for the rest of the regular season

Boerne Champion at Smithson Valley: The game scheduled for Oct. 23 is a Game of the Year candidate. Given how each team has dominated, especially in District 13-5A-I, this game should decide the league title. Smithson Valley is the state's top-ranked team in Class 5A Division I and has outscored opponents, 350-45 (303-31 in district) in going 5-0. Champion is ranked No. 6 and holds a 353-56 (231-35) scoring advantage with a 6-0 mark. Champion is quarterbacked by the nation's top ranked recruit for the 2029 class in sophomore Ryder Flugence. Smithson Valley has replenished on defense and might be better than the team that shut down the one of Texas' most prolific offenses in Frisco Lone Star, 28-6, in last year's state championship.

Johnson vs. Reagan: The significance of this game rests on Reagan's ability to maintain momentum after a rough start. This year's "Stone Oak Super Bowl" is set for Oct. 23 at Heroes Stadium. Johnson, the area's top-ranked team is 4-0, and tied for first place in District 28-6A with Reagan and Roosevelt at 2-0. The Rattlers have rebounded after massive losses against Steele (52-14) and Brennan (63-0). Since 2020, Johnson or Reagan has won the district title with the Jaguars winning in 2025, 2024 and 2021.

Brennan vs. Harlan: The Bears and Hawks appear to be on a collision course for the District 29-6A when they meet on Nov. 6 at Farris Stadium in their regular season finale. They are the lone undefeated teams remaining in district play. The winner of this game has won the district championship each season since 2022 (Harlan in 2025 and 2023).

McCollum vs. Harlandale: The 63rd edition of the Frontier Bowl, scheduled for Nov. 6 at Harlandale Memorial Stadium, could decide the District 14-5A-II title. Harlandale is 4-0 in district (4-2 overall) while the Cowboys are 3-0 in district (3-2 overall). A lot of things need to fall into place for that to happen, but it's plausible, and that's a big deal. The Indians haven't been to the playoffs since 2023 and the Cowboys last got there in 2015. The last time the Frontier Bowl decided a district title was 2004 when both were undefeated in league play.

On Tuesday, Atlético welcomed Mônica Hauck, CEO of Sólides, to Arena MRV for a meeting with the Club's leadership, including CEO Pedro Daniel. The initiative is part of Galo's leadership development program and aims to encourage the exchange of experiences and broaden perspectives on management, people, and business.

During the meeting, Mônica shared experiences from her time leading Sólides and offered insights into entrepreneurship, people management, and organizational culture, particularly amid the challenges of a constantly changing landscape.

Topics discussed included adapting to change, developing teams equipped for different scenarios, and the importance of a culture that encourages learning, innovation, and high performance.

The program, developed by Atlético's HR department, brings together Club leaders and executives from different sectors, connecting Galo with industry experiences and practices that can contribute to its staff's development and help address the challenges of football.

"Exchanging experiences is an important tool for development. Our goal is to create opportunities for our leaders to explore different perspectives, reflect on their own challenges, and broaden the knowledge they draw on when making decisions," says Sarah Lorentz, Atlético's Human Resources Manager.

The meeting reinforces the Club's commitment to the ongoing development of its leaders and to building a culture increasingly equipped to meet the challenges of the future.

articles.title: Former Texans Pro Bowl RB Joe Mixon’s weird injury saga continues after failed signing
articles.summary: Well, it looks like Joe Mixon won't be returning to the NFL after all.
articles.body:
Well, it looks like Joe Mixon won't be returning to the NFL after all.

After undergoing a team physical on Tuesday morning, the Seattle Seahawks have elected not to sign the former Houston Texans Pro Bowl running back to their practice squad.

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the team only planned to sign Mixon if it was contingent on passing the team's physical. Mixon did not play at all in 2025 due to a foot injury.

Mixon, 30, was released in March by the Texans after spending the entire season on their non-football injury list. Houston traded for David Montgomery from the Detriot Lions to replace Mixon following a year removed from his second Pro Bowl season.

In his lone year of playing for the franchise, Mixon rushed for 1,016 yards and 11 touchdowns, earning Pro Bowl honors. He also becme the first Texans running back since Carlos Hyde in 2019 to rush for 1,000 yards in a single season.

All last season, both Texans coach DeMeco Ryans and general manager Nick Caserio were highly secretive about Mixon's condition, often saying "he's progressing" or providing "no update at the time" comments about the starting running back.

Because of his departure, the run game was depleted. Houston averaged less than four yards per carry behind a combination of Woody Marks and Nick Chubb, with the rookie out of USC eventually becoming the focal point of the offensive ground game.

Over the weekend, Mixon posted a video of a workout that ended with him stating, "I'm back, baby!" Shortly after, the Seahawks invited him for a workout.

Seattle has been missing its top two running backs for most of the past two weeks. First-round pick Jadarian Price will miss at least three games after being placed on injured reserve with a chest injury before Week 4. Meanwhile, Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list, has been trying to return from his ACL tear suffered in last season's postseason run.

As for the Texans, while moving off Mixon felt like the right move, their ground game woes continue into 2026. Entering Sunday's matchup on the road, Houston ranks 30th in rushing yards (79.0 yards per game) and 29th in yards per attempt (3.5).

The Texans have four total rushing touchdowns, two from each lead back.

Kickoff in Nashville against the Tennessee Titans is scheduled for Noon on CBS.

articles.title: Here's a look at the highest and lowest winning percentage for players in fantasy football through four weeks
articles.summary: We break down the players popping up on the best and worst fantasy football teams after the first month of the season.
articles.body:
We've made it through the first four weeks of fantasy football in 2026. It's time to reflect on our rosters and decisions, plus look ahead to how we can continue our winning ways or fix a slow start to the season . Yahoo provided us with data highlighting which players have shown up most and least often on winning rosters through four weeks. Below, we'll break down the lists.

Highest Percentage of Players on Winning Rosters

It's no surprise to see the Chiefs' back at the top of this list after what he's done to opposing defenses over the first four weeks. The lowest Walker has finished in fantasy points on a weekly basis is RB4 as Kansas City enters its bye.

JSN is tracking toward leading the NFL in receiving yards for a second straight campaign with 481 through four games. Prior to Week 4, Smith-Njigba had at least eight catches for over 100 yards and a score in every contest, including a 9-155-3 outburst in Week 2 versus Arizona.

If you invested an ealry pick in Williams, he's been about as consistent as you can get so far in 2026. He posted double-digit fantasy totals in each of the first three weeks before breaking out with 31.7 points in Week 4 for an RB1 finish.

If you drafted Lamb this season, you likely got a discount after he spurned managers in 2025. The Cowboys' top receiver hasn't scored fewer than 12.9 fantasy points in a game so far this season, and has topped 30+ points on two separate occasions.

The consensus No. 1 overall pick has been just that in 2026 for a Lions team that continues to be a wealth of fantasy points for managers on both sides. Gibbs has cleared 19 touches in each game and has three games of 20+ fantasy points.

Lowest Percentage of Players on Winning Rosters

Most of the players on this list are here due to some type of injury. Brown posted only a 3-26-0 line on four targets in his Patriots debut in Week 1 and then was placed on injured reserve with an ankle issue.

We all suspected Achane would regress with a new coaching staff and low expectations for the Dolphins. That was the case through three weeks before Achane tore his ACL and was ruled out for the rest of 2026.

This is purely because Nacua has missed two of four games this season. He got to double-digit points in Week 1 before missing two weeks, but returned in Week 4 to post a solid 9-125-0 line on 12 targets while also scoring a rushing TD — what we're used to seeing from him.

After lighting the fantasy world on fire in 2024, it's been a rough year and change for Barkley, who is on the mend with a hamstring injury. He's had to exit early in two games this season and the Eagles offense has been disappointing to start the Sean Mannion era. To make matters worse, potential future Hall of Fame OT Lane Johnson just announced he's retiring.

Chase has two great games sandwiched between one quiet one and one where he left early due to injury. He's now dealing with a concussion that has his status for Week 5 up in the air. Chase's reign atop the fantasy WR ranks may be coming to an end in 2026.
